Q: replace() takes no keyword arguments, in for loop A:

The error is due to the fact that you are applying str.replace to a string and not to a column (Pandas.Series.replace) as intended because wo.columns returns the columns' labels and not the columns themselves (see pandas.DataFrame.columns).

Just change

for column in wo.columns[14:21]:
    column = column.replace( '[\$,)]','', regex=True)
    #        ^^^^^^ this is a string

to

for column in wo.columns[14:21]:
    wo[column] = wo[column].replace( '[\$,)]','', regex=True)
    #            ^^^^^^^^^^ this is a Series ✅

Here's a little demo:

import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "description": [
        "first item",
        "second item",
        "third item",
    ],
    "amount": ["10$", "200,000$", "3"]
})
df

# Output
#    description    amount
# 0   first item       10$
# 1  second item  200,000$
# 2   third item         3

for column in df.columns:
  print(f"column {column} is of type {type(column)}")
  print(f"df[{column}] is of type {type(df[column])}")
  df[column] = df[column].replace({r'[\$,)]': ''}, regex=True)

# Output
# column description is of type <class 'str'>
# df[description] is of type <class 'pandas.core.series.Series'>
# column amount is of type <class 'str'>

And a bit more elegant (and efficient) than the for loop:

df.iloc[:, [1]] = df.iloc[:, [1]].apply(
    lambda s: s.str.replace(r'[\$,)]', '', regex=True).astype(float)
)

# Output
#    description    amount
# 0   first item      10.0
# 1  second item  200000.0
# 2   third item       3.0
